item.title: Eyrie v0.2.0, and a new home for this site
item.description: Long day. Two things shipped: Eyrie v0.2.0, and this website on its own build. On Eyrie: A Gemini CLI adapter, so all three CLIs are in. First-run setup, and a UI driven by capabilities, so it only shows what the installed CLIs can actually do. Packaging: a PyInstaller build of the server, Tauri app bundles, and .dmg , .deb , .rpm and AppImage. Release CI install-tests each distro. A one-line install.sh , a Homebrew tap, and an MIT license. Then I tagged and released v0.2.0. After the release:

item.title: Eyrie finds my other terminals
item.description: Until today Eyrie only knew about sessions it started itself. Most of my sessions don’t start there. I open a terminal tab and run claude or codex like always. So now the widget lists sessions running in my own terminals, and the Sessions page shows Claude Code and Codex sessions running outside Eyrie too. Also today: Release builds for the widget, as a .app and a .dmg . An app icon. A high-level LLD doc. Per-CLI locks, so two actions on the same CLI can’t step on each other. Wider secret masking in anything Eyrie shows or logs. Next up: Gemini CLI support and proper packaging, so someone other than me can install it.

item.title: Eyrie gets a new look, and Linux
item.description: Sunday was mostly about how Eyrie looks. I restyled the whole app in a new design language: paper and ink colours, small mono eyebrows over each section. What else got done: /api/v1/summary , one endpoint that feeds both the home page and the widget. A systemd user service, so it runs on Ubuntu the same way the launchd agent does on macOS. A platform matrix design: macOS, Ubuntu and Fedora for now. Windows is deferred. Started the top-bar widget in Tauri. Next up: getting the widget to show sessions that I started outside Eyrie.

item.title: Eyrie, day one: a backend and a prototype
item.description: Started Eyrie today. It’s my own open-source control plane for the AI coding CLIs I use every day (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), and it runs locally. The code is at github.com/abrahamalen/eyrie . The first design had Docker in it. I dropped that early. Everything Eyrie needs is already on my laptop: the CLIs, their config files, their transcripts. A container would only get in the way, so it’s laptop-only.

item.title: Using Mermaid Diagrams in Technical Documentation
item.description: Diagrams are essential for explaining complex systems and processes in technical documentation. Mermaid makes it easy to create and maintain diagrams using a simple markdown-like syntax, directly in your content files. In this post, I’ll show several examples of diagrams you can create using Mermaid. Flowchart Example Let’s start with a basic flowchart showing a deployment process: The code to create this flowchart is surprisingly simple: flowchart TD A[Code Changes] --> B{Code Review} B -->|Approved| C[Build & Test] B -->|Rejected| A C --> D{Tests Pass?} D -->|Yes| E[Deploy to Staging] D -->|No| A E --> F{Staging Validation} F -->|Pass| G[Deploy to Production] F -->|Fail| A G --> H[Monitor] Sequence Diagram Example Sequence diagrams are perfect for showing interactions between components:

item.title: Creating My Digital Scrapbook
item.description: Today I added a proper Digital Scrapbook section to my website. This is a place where I can post shorter, more casual thoughts and updates compared to my regular blog posts. The implementation included: Creating a dedicated layout template for the scrapbook page Styling it with CSS to match the rest of my site’s aesthetic Adding a simple search functionality Setting up the proper directory structure for daily entries I’m planning to use this space to document quick learnings, interesting links I find, and progress on various projects. It feels good to have a low-pressure space to jot down thoughts without the formality of a full blog post.

item.title: Website Improvements - March 31, 2025
item.description: Today’s Website Improvements Made several significant improvements to the website today: Archives Page Added a “Dailies” section to the Archives page with a clean calendar icon Styled the link to align perfectly with the page design Removed “Daily Logs” from the main menu for cleaner navigation Home Page Redesign Completely revamped the home page layout Added “Also seen on:” section with aligned social media icons Improved spacing and typography across the page Made the layout more consistent with proper line heights Kept only important navigation links underlined for better visual hierarchy Added “Now” Page Created a new “Now” page to showcase current activities Implemented auto-updating timestamp using Git information Added professional focus, learning, reading, and projects sections Created a custom shortcode for timestamp display Overall, today’s changes focused on better organization, improved navigation, and a cleaner, more consistent design across the site.
